title: A Horizon for the Trail
premise: Marguerite Ashgrove has spent nine years running her riverboat the Kestrel up and down the Sarelle, outrunning debts, grief, and the memory of the family she lost when the nation of Vesseny collapsed. When a flood delivers a sealed chest stamped with Vesseny's royal crest into her hold, she becomes the unwilling custodian of a proof of succession that three factions — exiled loyalists, a mercantile syndicate, and a government minister — will kill to control. Sheltering a fugitive archivist named Tomas Reyes, Marguerite must run the river through monsoon, sabotage, and a betrayer aboard her own crew, racing to reach the high mountain pass before the glacier calving season opens the only route north. She learns the chest holds her own family's name, forcing her to choose between the duty of returning what is Vesseny's and the found family she has built on the water. In the end she opens the route, delivers the truth publicly instead of secretly, and chooses Tomas and her crew over the crown's restoration — finding that a horizon, not a homeland, is what she was always steering toward.
about_author: Ines Zhou is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons piloting cargo boats on glacial-fed waterways before turning to fiction. Her work blends nautical realism with quiet, character-driven adventure.

chapters.title: The Mood of the Water
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A routine cargo run up the Sarelle establishes the Kestrel, her loyal but fractious crew, and her rule: never stop moving. A near-miss with a sandbar shows her preternatural river-reading skill. Beat: competence masking restlessness.

chapters.title: What the Flood Brings Up
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. After a storm swell, the crew nets a waterlogged chest stamped with the extinct seal of Vesseny. Marguerite wants to sell it; first mate Odile insists on opening it. Inside: documents and a locket with a name Marguerite recognizes from her buried past. Beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Man in the Reeds
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A fugitive archivist, hunted by the syndicate, begs passage at a fueling dock. Marguerite refuses — until syndicate enforcers arrive and her instinct to protect overrides her instinct to flee. Beat: reluctant compassion.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Current
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Flashback woven into a night watch: her family's role in Vesseny's fall, the fire, the debt she owes a dead sister. Tomas begins decoding the documents; one names the Ashgrove line. Beat: the past stops being past.

chapters.title: Passengers and Liars
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A charming merchant, Callum Voss, charters passage north — secretly the syndicate's agent. Odile, hiding her own debts, lets him aboard without telling Marguerite. Beat: complicity and quiet guilt.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The rains close in early; the Kestrel takes on water and the crew must bail through the night, Tomas working alongside them. A moment of laughter in the flood — the first warmth between Marguerite and Tomas. Beat: found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Minister's Letter
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The documents prove a living heir to Vesseny's throne. A government minister offers Marguerite amnesty and a new boat if she surrenders the chest. She almost says yes. Beat: temptation of the easy exit.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The engine is fouled with river silt — deliberate. Suspicion tears at the crew; young deckhand Pirro is accused unjustly. Marguerite defends him, deepening her bond with the crew. Beat: loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Callum's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas discovers Voss's coded correspondence and realizes the syndicate plans to seize the Kestrel at the gorge. He tells Marguerite; she chooses not to throw Voss off — yet. Beat: cold strategy over hot anger.

chapters.title: The Leeches of Lowport
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A port stop to patch the hull becomes a trap: the syndicate has bought the harbormaster. A tense escape at night, running lights dark, with Odile's local knowledge saving them. Beat: the crew becomes a unit.

chapters.title: What Odile Owes
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Confession scene: Odile reveals she let Voss aboard to clear her debts. Marguerite's fury — then forgiveness, because she understands running from what you owe. Beat: forgiveness as the spine of found family.

chapters.title: The Gorge
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Voss makes his move at the narrow gorge; syndicate boats close in. Marguerite threads the Kestrel through rapids no hired pilot would dare, losing their pursuers but cracking the hull. Beat: triumph at the edge of disaster.

chapters.title: Stranded at Saint-Elm
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Hauled up on a shingle bank, the crew repairs the boat while waiting for the monsoon's end. Tomas and Marguerite admit, almost, what they feel. He offers her the choice: leave the chest, leave Vesseny behind. Beat: love against duty, stated plainly.

chapters.title: The Heir's Locket
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite finally opens her sister's letter inside the locket: the heir the documents name is Marguerite's niece, alive, in the northern settlements. The duty is no longer abstract. Beat: the personal cost of the past.

chapters.title: The Minister's Second Offer
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The minister intercepts them with gunboats and a darker offer: surrender the girl's claim, or the syndicate gets her. Marguerite refuses — and the minister reveals he knows about the glacier route and will be waiting. Beat: no way out but through.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The crew runs the minister's blockade at night, engines muffled, Pirro steering by starlight. A near-sinking; Odile saves Voss from drowning despite everything, and he begins to waver. Beat: grace under fire.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Choice
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss, moved by the crew's refusal to abandon him, burns his syndicate orders and gives them the syndicate's northern timetable. Marguerite accepts him warily into the fold. Beat: even the traitor can be found family.

chapters.title: The Calving Fields
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. They reach the glacier as the calving season opens — the route north is a shifting maze of ice and meltwater, open for weeks only. The minister's ship shadows them. Beat: awe and dread in equal measure.

chapters.title: Ice and Gunpowder
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Climax begins: the minister forces a confrontation in the ice channel. The Kestrel is holed; Marguerite lures the gunboat onto a calving face, sacrificing her beloved boat to save the crew. Beat: the captain gives up the thing she loves most.

chapters.title: The Girl on the Shore
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Shipwrecked survivors reach the northern settlement; Marguerite meets her niece, Ana, and gives her the documents — not as a crown, but as a choice. Ana chooses to tell the truth publicly rather than seize power. Beat: duty fulfilled by letting go.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Aftermath: the minister's faction collapses when the documents go public; the syndicate retreats. The crew, boatless, salvages the Kestrel's wheel and nameplate. Marguerite and Tomas finally speak plainly. Beat: grief and gratitude braided together.

chapters.title: A Horizon for the Trail
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. One year later: a new boat, the Kestrel II, crew intact, running the northern rivers with Ana occasionally aboard. Marguerite no longer runs from anything — she steers toward the horizon because she chooses to. Beat: arrival, not as a place, but as a way of moving.
